indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.4.1.2: Show understanding of the concept of heat energy in terms of its importance, effects, sources and transfer from one medium to another
indicator.objective: Explain the terms hot and cold

skills.description: Explain in simple words what 'hot' and 'cold' mean
Sort familiar items into hot and cold
Say what happens when something is heated or cooled

misconceptions: Cold is a kind of energy that comes from ice.
If it is not on fire, it is cold.
Hot and cold are the same as hard and soft.
Objects become cold by gaining coldness, not by losing heat.

questions.stem: Which of these is usually hot?
hints: It is very dangerous to touch.
questions.explanation: Fire is very hot.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think fire is cold.

questions.stem: Which of these is usually cold?
hints: It is kept in the fridge.
questions.explanation: Ice cream is cold because it is kept frozen.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all food is hot.

questions.stem: How does a hot cup of tea feel when you touch it?
questions.explanation: A hot cup of tea feels warm or hot to the touch.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse hot with just being wet.

questions.stem: When you touch a piece of ice, how does it feel?
hints: It makes your hand feel chilly.
questions.explanation: Ice feels cold to the touch.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think ice is hot because the sun melts it.

questions.stem: What is the main natural source of heat for the Earth?
hints: It gives us light during the day.
questions.explanation: The sun is the main natural source of heat.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the moon gives heat.

questions.stem: Ama is sorting items. Which group is all cold?
hints: Which group has things from the fridge/freezer?
The other groups have fire or heat.
questions.explanation: Ice, cold water, and an ice block are all cold items.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water is always cold.

questions.stem: Which of these is a source of heat at home?
questions.explanation: A stove is a source of heat used for cooking.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think only the sun gives heat.

questions.stem: What happens to an ice block when you leave it in the sun?
questions.explanation: An ice block melts when left in the sun because the heat turns it into liquid water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think ice stays solid in the sun.

questions.stem: What happens to water when you put it in a fridge?
questions.explanation: Water becomes cold when placed in a fridge.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fridge adds cold energy.

questions.stem: If something is NOT hot, we say it is...
hints: It is the opposite of hot.
questions.explanation: The opposite of hot is cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse temperature with texture (hard/soft).

questions.stem: Name one hot thing and one cold thing in your home.
answer: hot: fire/stove/iron, cold: ice/water in fridge
hints: What do you use to cook?
What do you use to cool a drink?
questions.explanation: A stove is hot, and ice is cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may list items that are room temperature.

questions.stem: Name one thing that gives us heat.
questions.explanation: The sun and fire are sources of heat.

questions.stem: Why do we put ice in a bottle of water on a hot day?
questions.explanation: We put ice in water to make it cold because ice is cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think ice adds flavor.

questions.stem: Kwame wants to make his water hot. Which of these can he use?
questions.explanation: An electric kettle is a source of heat used to boil water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a fan makes water hot.

questions.stem: What happens to a hot iron when you unplug it and leave it for a long time?
hints: It is no longer connected to electricity.
questions.explanation: The hot iron cools down when unplugged because it loses heat to the air.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the iron stays hot forever.

questions.stem: Explain how you can tell if something is hot or cold just by touching it.

criteria.description: States that hot things feel warm or burning
States that cold things feel chilly or cool

questions.explanation: We use our sense of touch to feel if something is hot (warm/burning) or cold (chilly/cool).

questions.stem: Which of these is true about a boiling pot of water and a piece of ice?
options: The water is hot and the ice is cold
The water is cold and the ice is hot
questions.explanation: Boiling water is hot, and ice is cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may confuse the two states.

questions.stem: Why does a metal spoon left in a hot cup of tea feel hot after some time?
options: The tea is hot and the heat moves to the spoon
The spoon makes its own heat
hints: The spoon is in the hot tea.
Heat moves from the tea to the spoon.
questions.explanation: The heat from the hot tea moves to the metal spoon, making the spoon feel hot.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think the spoon generates heat.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT a source of heat?
questions.explanation: A block of ice is not a source of heat; it is cold.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think all solids give off heat.

questions.stem: Tell me one thing that is hot and one thing that is cold, and explain how you know.

criteria.description: Names a hot object and says it feels warm/burning
Names a cold object and says it feels chilly/cool

questions.explanation: This tests the understanding of hot and cold through touch.
